bug_description.normalized: The staged 6056-byte malformed ELF reaches libdwarf's GNU debuglink handling. Static inspection of the saved `poc` shows a `.gnu_debuglink` section with 8 bytes `00 00 00 8d 00 07 1d 00`, so the section name begins with a NUL byte and is therefore the empty string. `_dwarf_extract_debuglink()` accepts that layout because `_dwarf_check_string_valid()` only requires a NUL before section end, `strlen(ptr)` yields `namelen == 0`, and the derived `(crcptr + 4) == endptr` check still passes for the 8-byte section. It returns a non-null pointer to the empty name, and `dwarf_gnu_debuglink()` passes that pointer into `_dwarf_construct_linkedto_path()`. The latter treats any non-null `link_string_in` as present, initializes `joind.js_linkstring` as a `dwarfstring` backed by the global literal `""`, and then appending the empty input leaves that backing unchanged because the append path sees zero length and performs no copy. `prepare_linked_name()` first copies the executable directory into the output path, so `_dwarf_pathjoinl()` later sees a non-empty target and calls `is_full_path(inputs, joinchar)` on the still-empty link string instead of returning early. In the vulnerable source, `is_full_path()` reads `path[1]` without rejecting empty strings first. That dereferences one byte past the global empty-string literal from `dwarf_string.c`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ at `src/lib/libdwarf/dwarf_debuglink.c:81` in `is_full_path`.

source.description: First scored project parser step that consumes the attacker-controlled `.gnu_debuglink` bytes as a candidate string and admits the empty-name witness.
source.value_from: The staged `gt_results/arvo_47150/poc` has sha256 `41ad6e808821fdcd8dd8dce36040f6f21f9af35a6729d7086395c1541318096b` and size 6056. Static `readelf -x .gnu_debuglink` on that file shows the section bytes `00 00 00 8d 00 07 1d 00`: byte 0 is the NUL terminator of an empty string, and the section length is still 8 bytes. `_dwarf_check_string_valid()` therefore sees `ptr < endptr` and finds a terminating NUL immediately at `ptr[0]`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `is_full_path()` reads the second byte of the path argument even when the argument is the global empty-string literal, causing the recorded one-byte global over-read.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `global-buffer-overflow on address ... READ of size 1` at `is_full_path /src/libdwarf/src/lib/libdwarf/dwarf_debuglink.c:81:10`, and the report identifies the touched object as the 1-byte global string literal `""` defined in `dwarf_string.c:71`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `is_full_path()` assumes the input path has at least two bytes and dereferences `path[1]` without first rejecting the empty-string case.
root_cause.note: The staged fix adds `if (!c) return FALSE;` before this read and also adds `if (!c1) return FALSE;` before the `':'` test, making the empty-string and one-character cases explicit.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the accepted `.gnu_debuglink` name becomes the `debuglink_path_returned` string later passed as `link_string_in` into `_dwarf_construct_linkedto_path()`.

parser_admitted.description: The malformed file has already been opened as a DWARF object, its `.gnu_debuglink` section has nonzero size and has been loaded, and libdwarf is now extracting that section instead of rejecting the file earlier.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false and there is no `trace_feedback.json`, so Stage 02 stayed source-grounded and did not add instrumentation.
Stage 02 does not execute the fixed tree, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though the staged patch adds the missing empty-string guards in `is_full_path()`.

The staged `poc` is a heavily malformed ELF and generic `readelf` emits many unrelated header warnings. The trigger contract below is therefore grounded only in the observed `.gnu_debuglink` bytes, the staged vulnerable source, and the saved ASan/reproduction artifacts.

fine_trace.note: Source. `_dwarf_extract_debuglink()` treats the staged `.gnu_debuglink` bytes as a C string. The witness section begins with `0x00`, so this helper accepts the empty name because it only checks that some NUL terminator exists before `endptr`.
The accepted debuglink name is measured as length 0. That emptiness is the value later preserved through path construction.

Even with `namelen == 0`, the debuglink record is not rejected. For this witness the section length is 8 bytes, so the derived CRC pointer lands at byte 4 and the `(crcptr + 4) == endptr` check passes.
The accepted empty string is exported as `debuglink_path_returned`. `dwarf_gnu_debuglink()` later passes this exact non-null empty pointer as `link_string_in` into `_dwarf_construct_linkedto_path()`.
The path-building branch is taken because step 4 produced a non-null pointer, even though the pointed-to string is empty. There is no emptiness check here.

`construct_js()` initialized `joind.js_linkstring` with `dwarfstring_constructor()` so its storage starts as the global literal `""` (`dwarf_string.c:69-74`). Appending step 4's empty string computes zero length and `dwarfstring_append_length()` returns immediately on `slen == 0` (`dwarf_string.c:167-175`), so `joind.js_linkstring` still points to that same global `""`.
`prepare_linked_name()` first copies the executable directory into `out`. This makes the destination path non-empty before `_dwarf_pathjoinl(out, linkname)` is called on step 6's empty link string.

Because step 7 already made `target` non-empty, `_dwarf_pathjoinl()` does not take its `!targlen` early return. It reaches the `is_full_path(inputs, joinchar)` call with `inputs = dwarfstring_string(input)` still pointing to step 6's global `""`.

Root cause and sink. `is_full_path()` never checks whether `path[0]` is NUL before reading `path[1]`. With step 8 calling it on the global empty-string literal still backing `joind.js_linkstring`, this statement reads one byte past the 1-byte `""` object and ASan reports the saved global-buffer-overflow READ.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: not applicable: ASan reports a global-buffer-overflow on the dwarfstring empty-string literal, not a heap allocation context

poc.trigger: PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_47150 run --version vulnerable --expect crash

format.name: malformed ELF with empty .gnu_debuglink
format.contract: The object must still reach `dwarf_gnu_debuglink()` with a loadable `.gnu_debuglink` section whose name field is the empty string (`section[0] == 0`) while the section length still satisfies `_dwarf_extract_debuglink()`'s `(crcptr + 4) == endptr` check. For the saved witness this is the 8-byte section `00 00 00 8d 00 07 1d 00`, which yields a non-null empty `link_string_in` that reaches `_dwarf_pathjoinl()`.
